title: The Cotton Pickers break up in Detroit over unpaid wages
summary: Because the band was not being paid, the bass player hid the music and demanded his back pay, and the band broke up in Detroit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Why did they break up, were you with them when they broke up?
Oh yes, I was there. Well, money.

And so bass player was the first to leave, so he took all -- somehow or other he got hold to the music. He took all the music and hid it. So we didn't have anything -- we could've faked, but McKinney wanted his music. That was why the band broke up and this bass player kept the music and called Mac and says Mac you want your music you got to pay me what you owe me, and so Mac --
sent him the money so he told him the music right up in my attic so you go get it. He says, I'm gone. So he left. And that's when the band broke up. Bennie left and I left.
I came right along to New York.
Where was the band when it broke up?
